subject: enabling KnowledgeReuseGate (runtime.knowledge_reuse.enabled)

current_state.observed_runtime_effect: stage reports NO_RUN / DISABLED every cycle

gates_that_are_not_met.coverage: 876 of 2090 tasks; 0 of the 944 tasks created 10-17..10-18
gates_that_are_not_met.consequence: even with the flag set, the gate would refuse the stale index

gates_that_are_not_met.gate: labelled query set for quantitative A/B
gates_that_are_not_met.consequence: SOURCE_OF_TRUTH section 7 records this as an open item; without it the A/B gate is REVIEW_REQUIRED

why_not: The gate is deliberately fail-closed and its own precondition is currently unmet. Enabling the flag would not make reuse work - it would make reuse *look* enabled while refusing to run, which is worse than an honest DISABLED because the report would stop being a signal.

The index was built 2026-10-09 and no cycle rebuilds it; ops/build_knowledge_join_index.py exists but nothing in the daemon calls it. Enabling now would additionally require first wiring that builder, which is a change in its own right and needs its own acceptance path.

source docs (SOURCE_OF_TRUTH section 4/7, AGENTS.md memory-path truth 2026-10-02) both state the reuse stage is dry-run by design pending independent evidence. Nothing in this audit produced that evidence.

Reuse attaches evidence to new tasks. Attaching stale or unvalidated evidence is worse than attaching none, because a reused pointer can satisfy a validator's independence count - which is the exact failure this audit found in the task-card ring.
what_would_change_this: Wire ops/build_knowledge_join_index.py into a scheduled path so the index stops ageing, and prove it by showing coverage of tasks created since the last build.
Assemble the labelled query set and run ops/assess_memory_index_migration.py to a real A/B verdict rather than REVIEW_REQUIRED.
Only then set enabled=true, and keep mode=dry-run for the first cycle so the gate reports plans without attaching.
